Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can align internally: 

- Volume ranges you mentioned: pilot 50M tokens / month, target production ~400–600M tokens / month (spikes up to ~1B/month in peak months). Please confirm if that still looks right.
- Primary workload: stream + chat generation (avg prompt+response length ~1.2k tokens).
- Target unit economics you called out: roughly $10–$15 per 1M tokens.

Notes on regional/residency cost impact (high-level):
- Baseline hosted US region (multi-tenant Redwood API) is generally the most cost-effective; sample retail gen price we use starting is ~$18 / 1M tokens for this model class.
- EU-hosted endpoints typically carry an infrastructure and compliance premium (roughly +15–25% depending on sizing and egress patterns). That uplift is mainly network/infra, regional capacity premiums, and GDPR-related operational controls.
- If you require strict EU-only data residency and audit controls (customer-managed KMS or Private deployment), that often pushes customers to our Dedicated or Private options and adds platform/ops cost (one-time onboarding & a modest monthly platform fee). That can be offset with committed capacity discounts.

Attached: initial_estimate.csv (very rough). I can produce a usage-model spreadsheet with committed vs PAYG scenarios once you confirm: (a) average monthly tokens, (b) target SLO/latency region (US vs EU), and (c) appetite for a 6–12 month committed commitment.

Next steps we discussed:
1) You confirm the expected steady-state monthly tokens and whether EU residency is required.
2) We’ll run three scenarios: PAYG (hosted), Dedicated reserved (6mo/12mo), and Private (if residency/controls required) with per-1M token unit economics.
3) Block a 30-min follow-up next week with your VP Eng + Procurement to review the delta and procurement timing.

If helpful I can ballpark a committed price range today once you confirm the monthly volume band — happy to do that in this thread.

Thanks,

Great context — thanks Alex. Below are conservative ballparks so you have something to share with Procurement while we run the exact model:

PAYG (hosted, no commitment):
- US region (hosted API): ~ $18 / 1M tokens (typical for this model class w/ streaming/chat workloads).
- EU region (hosted API): ~ $21.5 / 1M tokens (~+20% uplift vs US) — drives from regional infra costs and PKI/KMS ops differences.

Committed / Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity, committed over 12 months):
- Typical committed discounts bring effective unit price down to ~$9–$13 / 1M depending on commitment size and model efficiency.
- At ~500M tokens/month, a 12-month reservation often gets into the low teens or high single digits per 1M tokens.

Private (EU-only residency, VPC/on-prem):
- Expect platform/setup fees (one-time onboarding + minimal monthly platform fee). The per-1M token compute cost can be close to Dedicated if you run similar reserved capacity, but there is an ops premium for strict residency (we should model this explicitly).

Notes on what drives the EU uplift:
- Regional capacity premiums (fewer pooled spot opportunities), higher egress/cross-region charges, and additional encryption/KMS integration work for customer-managed keys.

Preliminary recommendation for Procurement messaging:
- If budget target is ~$12 / 1M, committed Dedicated (12-mo) is the most realistic route. PAYG in EU will be above that target given the uplift.

I attached an updated token-model workbook with the three scenarios (PAYG US/EU, Dedicated 6/12mo, Private residency). See 20260302_fintechco_token_model.xlsx (spreadsheet stub) and a PDF summary redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf. I’ll also drop the HubSpot deal with these scenarios: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FT-2026-042

Would you be available for a 30-min call on Wed or Thu this week to walk Procurement through the committed numbers? If you confirm the 60/40 EU/US split we can produce blended effective $/1M and a draft SOW for dedicated capacity.
